ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset inference from short windows with a conditional policy
PROPOSAL: Train a TD3+BC policy on D4RL hopper-medium-replay, halfcheetah-medium and walker2d-medium-expert, augmenting training observations with synthetic per-dimension offsets drawn from step, ramp and random-walk series. A 2-layer GRU encoder reads the last 10 observation-action pairs and outputs a latent offset estimate that conditions the actor and critic. At test time, evaluate on 6 unseen series: sawtooth, regime switches, seasonal sinusoids with jumps, heavy-tailed bursts, logged sensor traces and a non-Markovian autoregressive process. Report normalized return over the first 20 steps and over the episode, with 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: vanilla TD3+BC; TD3+BC trained with Gaussian observation noise; an adversarially robust baseline; a policy given the true offset; the encoder without action inputs
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The encoder recovers most of the true-offset return on step and ramp series and degrades on heavy-tailed bursts, where estimates stay biased early in the episode.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset recovery on locomotion benchmarks with critic ensembles
PROPOSAL: Train IQL on 9 D4RL locomotion datasets (hopper, halfcheetah and walker2d at medium, medium-replay and medium-expert levels) with offset augmentation from step and random-walk series. A transformer encoder over the last 10 observation-action pairs feeds an estimate to the actor, while the critic is an ensemble of 10 networks. Retrain the encoder at 3 widths and 3 context lengths, then test on 4 series: sawtooth, regime switches, seasonal jumps and bursts. Report normalized return over the episode and in the first 20 steps with 8 seeds, plus the offset error of the encoder.
CONTROLS: vanilla IQL; IQL trained with Gaussian noise; a policy given the true offset; encoders trained with 3 loss weightings; a variant without action inputs
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Wider encoders and longer contexts improve return on step series by a few points but saturate at moderate width; bursts remain hard for all variants.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Navigation offset estimation from forward-model prediction error
PROPOSAL: Train IQL on the D4RL datasets antmaze-medium-diverse, antmaze-large-play and maze2d-large, then fit a forward model on clean data and use its one-step prediction error over a window of 15 steps to infer a per-dimension offset. The estimate enters the actor through a 2-layer adapter with learning rate 3e-4 trained on augmented data from 4 synthetic series families. Test on 5 held-out series: square wave, drifting staircase, bursts, long-memory autoregressive and replayed calibration logs. Measure success rate in the first 30 steps and over the episode, with 10 seeds with offset error of the adapter logged at 3 checkpoints.
CONTROLS: IQL without adaptation; IQL trained with noise augmentation; a recurrent policy trained on offset-augmented data; a policy given the true offset; an adapter trained on one series family only
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Success rate rises over the noise-augmented baseline on staircase and square-wave series; the estimator fails when a drift is slow enough to be absorbed by the forward model's tolerance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Window-length sensitivity of offset estimation on Maze2D
PROPOSAL: Train IQL on the maze2d-large dataset, then fit a forward model on clean data and infer the offset from its one-step error over a window of length L, sweeping L from 5 to 40 and the adapter learning rate over 4 values. The adapter is trained on augmented data from 3 series families and the policy is tested on 4 held-out series: square wave, staircase pattern, bursts and autoregressive processes. Success rate is measured in the first 30 steps and over the episode with 10 seeds at all settings, refitting the forward model from scratch for 3 of the seeds, and a plot of success against window length is produced.
CONTROLS: IQL without adaptation; IQL trained with noise augmentation; a recurrent policy trained on offset-augmented data; a policy given the true offset as an input
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Success improves up to windows near 15 and flattens beyond; learning-rate choice matters scarcely once the window is long enough.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset-conditioned behavior regularization on Adroit hammer
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a pretrained TD3+BC policy on D4RL hammer-cloned and pen-human by adding an offset-estimation head trained with a 5-step prediction loss on clean transitions shifted by synthetic offsets, and log the estimation error of the head at episode start. At test time the head reads the first 8 observations and its output is subtracted from the incoming state before the policy acts. Evaluate on 4 unseen series (jump-and-hold, sinusoid, bursts, autoregressive) with 5 seeds, reporting normalized score at episode start and at episode end.
CONTROLS: unmodified TD3+BC; TD3+BC trained with Gaussian input noise; subtraction of the true offset; a head trained without shifted data
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Subtraction recovers a large share of the true-offset score on jump-and-hold and sinusoid series; it fails on bursts because 8 observations cannot separate a burst from state motion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offset subtraction heads across manipulation and locomotion suites
PROPOSAL: Train CQL, IQL and TD3+BC policies on 8 D4RL datasets drawn from hammer, pen, door, relocate, hopper and kitchen tasks, adding an offset-estimation head trained with prediction loss over horizons from 1 to 10 steps. At test time the head reads the first 8 observations and its output is subtracted from incoming states. Evaluate on 4 unseen series (jump-and-hold, sinusoid, bursts, autoregressive) with 3 seeds, reporting normalized score at episode start and at episode end for the algorithms.
CONTROLS: unmodified versions of the algorithms; versions trained with Gaussian input noise; subtraction of the true offset; a head trained without shifted data
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Head-based subtraction behaves alike for the 3 algorithms, with the same ordering of series difficulty; bursts remain the weak case at all horizons, and cross-suite differences in the ordering are small.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Streaming evaluation of history-based offset forecasting over 200-episode deployments
PROPOSAL: Train IQL and CQL backbones on antmaze-large-diverse, kitchen-mixed, hopper-medium-replay and walker2d-medium-expert, plus a sequence model trained on 50000 synthetic offset series from 12 generator families (steps, ramps, regime switching, seasonal, heavy tailed, long-memory, replayed logs). At deployment the agent sees a stream of 200 episodes with an optional history of the 20 most recent past offsets and forecasts the upcoming offset before acting, falling back to in-episode estimation when no history exists. Report return over the first 25 steps and the full episode, with 10 seeds.
CONTROLS: backbones without adaptation; last-value and moving-average forecasts of the past offsets; a recurrent policy trained on augmented data; in-episode estimation only; true offsets supplied
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The learned forecaster beats last-value on regime-switching and seasonal streams, ties on slow ramps, and loses on abrupt jumps where any extrapolation is wrong.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Forecaster capacity study on two locomotion datasets
PROPOSAL: Train IQL on hopper-medium-replay and walker2d-medium-expert, plus sequence-model forecasters of capacities from 2M to 120M parameters trained on 50000 synthetic offset series from generator families (steps, ramps, regime switching, seasonal, heavy tailed, long-memory). At deployment the agent sees a stream of 200 episodes with a history of the 20 most recent past offsets and forecasts the upcoming offset before acting. Report return over the first 25 steps and the full episode with 10 seeds, re-drawing the stream with new seeds, alongside forecast error of the sequence model on held-out series.
CONTROLS: IQL without adaptation; last-value and moving-average forecasts; a recurrent policy trained on augmented data; true offsets supplied
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Return improves with capacity up to roughly 30M parameters and flattens thereafter; regime-switching streams show the biggest gain over last-value.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibrating policies with a clean-data belief filter
PROPOSAL: Learn from the D4RL halfcheetah-medium-expert and ant-medium-replay datasets an ensemble of 5 transition models, then run a particle filter over the offset vector with 64 particles during test episodes, initialising from a broad prior and resampling when the effective sample size falls below 50%. The policy, trained with TD3+BC on offset-augmented data, acts on the corrected state. Test on 5 unseen series types: sawtooth, regime switches, bursts, seasonal drift and non-Markovian autoregression. Report normalized return from the first step and total return, with 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: unmodified TD3+BC; TD3+BC with noise training; a Kalman-style filter with a Gaussian random-walk offset; a policy given the true offset; the filter built on only one transition model
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The particle filter outperforms the Kalman variant on regime switches and bursts but is slower to converge on seasonal drift; early-episode return remains below the true-offset policy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Particle filtering of offsets on 6 locomotion datasets with varied ensemble sizes
PROPOSAL: Learn from D4RL datasets (halfcheetah, ant and hopper at medium-replay and medium-expert levels) transition-model ensembles from 3 to 20 members, then run a particle filter over the offset vector with 64 to 1024 particles during test episodes, logging filtering error at the start of test episodes and the correlation between error and return, and comparing resampling thresholds in the filter. The TD3+BC policy, trained on offset-augmented data, acts on the corrected state. Test on 5 series types: sawtooth, regime switches, bursts, seasonal drift and autoregression. Report normalized return from the first step and total return, with 8 seeds.
CONTROLS: unmodified TD3+BC; TD3+BC with noise training; a Kalman-style filter; a policy given the true offset as an input; a filter built on one transition model
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Return saturates at moderate ensemble and particle counts; larger settings change normalized return by under a point.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Zero-history baseline: calibrating the first steps with a linear offset probe
PROPOSAL: On D4RL walker2d-medium and hopper-medium, train a TD3+BC policy and fit a ridge-regression probe that maps the first 5 observed states to the offset, using clean trajectories shifted by 3 families of synthetic offsets. The probe output is subtracted from observations for the rest of the episode. Evaluate on 4 held-out series (steps, sinusoid, bursts, autoregressive) with 10 seeds, reporting normalized return and mean absolute offset error across the series. Comparing probe-based subtraction against a policy fed the raw shifted state isolates what early observations can reveal.
CONTROLS: raw shifted observations; the true offset subtracted; subtraction of the training-set mean offset; a probe fit on shuffled labels
COST: 24
PREDICTION: The probe removes most of the error for step and sinusoid series with 5 steps of context; bursts and autoregressive series stay near the raw baseline, which shows the limit of linear readout.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probe architecture comparison on Walker2d with offset subtraction
PROPOSAL: On D4RL walker2d-medium, train a TD3+BC policy and fit probes of these types (ridge, kernel ridge, shallow and deep MLPs, gradient boosting, GRU, temporal convolution, small transformer) that map the first 5 observed states to the offset, using clean trajectories shifted by 3 families of synthetic offsets. The probe output is subtracted from observations for the rest of the episode. Evaluate on 4 held-out series (steps, sinusoid, bursts, autoregressive) with 10 seeds, reporting normalized return and mean absolute offset error, and the probe training loss curves are inspected.
CONTROLS: raw shifted observations; the true offset subtracted; subtraction of the training-set mean offset; a probe fit on shuffled labels
COST: 24
PREDICTION: All probe types land within a few points of one another on step series, so architecture choice changes slightly for early readout.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diffusion-policy backbone with shift-invariant representation learning
PROPOSAL: Train a diffusion policy on D4RL kitchen-complete, kitchen-partial and adroit door-human with a contrastive loss that makes the state embedding invariant to additive shifts drawn from a broad augmentation set (steps, ramps, random walks, bursts). A 12M-parameter encoder processes the observation, and a lightweight head estimates the residual shift from the first 12 observations. Test on 6 held-out series including non-Markovian autoregressive and abrupt regime switching, with 5 seeds, reporting task completion and return over the first 20 steps.
CONTROLS: a diffusion policy trained without the invariance loss; the same policy with Gaussian noise augmentation; TD3+BC; true shift supplied as input; the invariance loss with the estimation head removed
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Invariance cuts early-episode degradation on step and ramp shifts; the benefit shrinks on bursts, which create inconsistencies the embedding cannot absorb.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling invariant encoders for offset-robust diffusion policies
PROPOSAL: Train diffusion policies on D4RL tasks (kitchen-complete, kitchen-partial, kitchen-mixed, door-human, pen-human, hammer-human, relocate-human) with a contrastive loss that makes the state embedding invariant to additive shifts drawn from step, ramp, random-walk and burst augmentations. Encoders from 12M to 200M parameters are compared, along with 3 loss weights; a lightweight head estimates the residual shift from the first 12 observations. Test on 6 held-out series with 5 seeds, reporting task completion and return over the first 20 steps, and the similarity between embeddings of shifted and clean states is reported with the benefit broken down by series type.
CONTROLS: a diffusion policy trained without the invariance loss; the same policy with Gaussian noise augmentation; TD3+BC; true shift supplied as input
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Larger encoders add only slightly beyond 50M parameters, and loss weight changes completion by under 3 points.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Offline pretraining on wear-style drift with conservative value learning
PROPOSAL: Train CQL on D4RL ant-medium and halfcheetah-medium-replay in which a slow wear model is simulated by adding a growing offset to the logged observations, with 3 growth laws (linear, saturating, step-wise) and per-dimension signs sampled at random. The actor receives the current observation and the difference to the first observation of the episode. Evaluate on abrupt non-Markovian series and on calibration-reset patterns never seen in training, reporting return in the first 15 steps and over the whole episode with 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: CQL on clean data; CQL with Gaussian noise augmentation; CQL trained on abrupt shifts directly; a policy given the true offset
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Training on smooth drift transfers poorly to abrupt resets, with return near the clean baseline in the first steps; training on abrupt shifts directly does better, which would show that the shift family matters more than breadth.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Seed and horizon analysis of drift-trained CQL on Ant
PROPOSAL: Train CQL on D4RL ant-medium with a simulated wear offset added to logged observations, using 3 growth laws (linear, saturating, step-wise) and random per-dimension signs. The actor receives the current observation and its difference to the first observation of the episode. Evaluate on abrupt non-Markovian series and calibration-reset patterns, reporting return in the first 15 steps and over the whole episode with 5 seeds, then repeat training from 3 dataset shuffles and 6 conservatism weights to check that conclusions persist.
CONTROLS: CQL on clean data; CQL with Gaussian noise augmentation; CQL trained on abrupt shifts directly; a policy given the true offset; the actor given only the current observation
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Conclusions persist over shuffles: return is near the clean baseline on resets, and conservatism weights between 1 and 10 move return by a few points at most.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretrained world model for offset inference across manipulation suites
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 100M-parameter transformer world model on the D4RL kitchen, adroit and antmaze collections, then use its latent states to infer per-dimension offsets online through gradient-based inversion of the observation shift over a window of 25 steps. The policy is IQL trained on augmented data from 10 generator families. Deployment streams run 100 episodes, and the agent may receive a history of 10 past offsets. Report return over the first 20 steps and the full episode, with 10 seeds, on 8 held-out series.
CONTROLS: IQL; a recurrent policy; a filter on the world model without gradient inversion; true offsets supplied
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Inversion beats the filter on abrupt regime switches because latent states disambiguate shifted observations; it degrades when the test suite differs strongly from the pretraining data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large-model offset inversion with re-run seeds on 3 suites
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 100M-parameter and 400M-parameter transformer world models on the D4RL kitchen, adroit and antmaze collections, then use latent states to infer per-dimension offsets online through gradient-based inversion over windows from 10 to 50 steps. The policy is IQL trained on augmented data from 10 generator families. Deployment streams run 100 episodes with a history of past offsets. Report return over the first 20 steps and the full episode, with 10 seeds, on 8 held-out series, and report offset error of the inversion at the start of test episodes and after long contexts.
CONTROLS: IQL; a recurrent policy; a filter on the world model without gradient inversion; true offsets supplied
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The 400M model improves return over the 100M model by under 2 points; window length 25 is about as good as 50.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Coverage limits of offset recovery on Maze2D
PROPOSAL: Subsample D4RL maze2d-medium to 10%, 30% and 100% of its trajectories, train IQL on all 3 subsamples, and fit a small MLP that regresses the offset from the first 6 observations using augmented clean data. Evaluate on 3 unseen series (square wave, sinusoid, autoregressive) with 5 seeds, reporting success rate and offset error across the series. The goal is to see whether recovery degrades because offsets push observations outside the support of the data. A diagnostic plot of estimation error against distance to the nearest training state accompanies the results.
CONTROLS: IQL on the full data without adaptation; IQL with noise augmentation; subtraction of the true offset; a regressor fit on shuffled labels
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Error grows with the distance to the nearest training state, and the 10% subsample loses success rate quickly under square-wave shifts; at 100% the regressor holds up for sinusoids.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Estimator comparison for Maze2D offsets with varied initial states
PROPOSAL: Train IQL on D4RL maze2d-medium, and fit offset regressors of 6 kinds (ridge, random forest, 1-layer MLP, 3-layer MLP, GRU, small transformer) from the first 6 observations using augmented clean data. Evaluate on 3 unseen series (square wave, sinusoid, autoregressive) with 3 seeds, reporting success rate and offset error, and train the regressors from 5 initial states to characterize variance, comparing them by training time and by sensitivity to input scaling. A summary table of estimation error against regressor kind accompanies the results.
CONTROLS: IQL without adaptation; IQL with noise augmentation; subtraction of the true offset; a regressor fit on shuffled labels
COST: 40
PREDICTION: The 6 regressors differ by under 3 points of success rate on sinusoids; spread among initial states exceeds the gap between most kinds.
